target: owned disposable postgres:16-alpine container per pass, destroyed
divergence_decision_convention: a '## D-NNNN' section of docs/decisions-and-divergences.md that names the code; accepted only if the section holds a line starting « Statut : acceptée par l'utilisateur le AAAA-MM-JJ », otherwise documented with the user's acceptance requested; one such line accepts every code its section names, so a partial acceptance needs its own section for the accepted codes

jsonb_key_order_normalized.pocketbase_0_22_34: v0.22.34 tools/types/json_raw.go:26-32: a json value served with its stored key order

number_served_as_text.pocketbase_0_22_34: v0.22.34 models/record.go:50-58 and models/schema/schema_field.go:312-343: the text of a SQLite integer or real is valid JSON, so a json field serves a JSON number

sqlite_integer_boolean_served_as_boolean.pocketbase_0_22_34: SQLite has no boolean storage class: TRUE, FALSE and comparisons are the integers 1 and 0 (https://www.sqlite.org/datatype3.html, 2.1); v0.22.34 models/schema/schema_field.go:312-343 serves them as the numbers 1 and 0

container_memory.interpretation: memory.peak and memory.current include the reclaimable page cache: cgroup 'file' (which also counts shmem). The memory that cannot be reclaimed without swap is anon + shmem (PostgreSQL shared_buffers is shmem). memory.events 'max' counts reclaims at the limit; 'oom' and 'oom_kill' must stay 0.

proves: every record of the real backup imported in one transaction into a disposable PostgreSQL built by the BUMA migrations; counts per table equal to the diagnosis
per-table fingerprints of the CONVERTED source rows (the importer's digest taken before COPY) equal to the committed rows re-read in a new session
source rowids archived for every table and kept as native rowid for users and buma_article
the three maxSelect-null relations stored as arrays equal to the raw SQLite lists, element for element and in order
orphan relations and references to absent files imported as they are and recounted

accounts (identity, hash, token key, auth dates) and the PocketBase admin (with created, updated and lastResetSentAt) equal to the raw source in their columns and the import archives; token secrets and mapped settings equal to the source
schema unchanged by the import apart from the two import archives (indexes and view bodies included); every view queryable, rows and distinct IDs equal to SQLite

values served over HTTP for the compared records equal the PocketBase 0.22.34 serialization of the raw SQLite values (model independent of the importer; unmodeled values counted apart, views in served_values.views_not_compared left out), except the divergences listed in http.divergences; user acceptance still requested for: jsonb_key_order_normalized (D-0029), number_served_as_text (D-0039), sqlite_integer_boolean_served_as_boolean (D-0039)

an isolated PPBase server serves the imported data with PocketBase 0.22.34 envelopes, totals, rules, error bodies, filters, expand, sort and file statuses on every sampled read (no rule left unverified; data, accounts and schema unchanged by the server and the reads), except the divergences listed in http.divergences; user acceptance still requested for: jsonb_key_order_normalized (D-0029), number_served_as_text (D-0039), sqlite_integer_boolean_served_as_boolean (D-0039)
the run is repeatable: two complete passes give identical aggregates, fingerprints and stored row hashes
does_not_prove: file bytes: no storage/ on this server; byte-for-byte copy is proven on the synthetic fixture and must be repeated with the complete archive
token continuity on real accounts: proven on the synthetic fixture (WS-C report)
the order of multi-element relation arrays: every real array holds at most one element; order is proven on the synthetic fixture (docs/c11-rehearsal-report.json)

values of the records not read over HTTP: page 1 by id of every collection and every record of the multiple-relation and auth collections are compared; the rest only through the importer's digest of the converted rows
served values of the views whose IDs are duplicated or null: their rows and distinct IDs are compared with SQLite, their records are not (http.served_values.views_not_compared)

which row a ROW_NUMBER() OVER () view ID names: neither engine defines that order; those views are compared as multisets of records, IDs aside (http.served_values.row_number_views_compared_as_multisets)
text sort order on a glibc or ICU PostgreSQL: this target (musl) sorts bytes like SQLite; a glibc en_US.UTF-8 target changes the order (count in http.sort)
desktop, mobile and SDK clients against this data
write routes, hooks and realtime on the imported data
production: no production server, backup freshness or cutover window is involved
the target PostgreSQL configuration and collation of production

privacy_check.method: patterns and 64-bit keys of every distinct text value of the snapshot
